title: Dual-quantile PoP orchestrator with network-integrity weighting and hysteresis
creator: Liam Chen
description: Problem: Production inference traffic sometimes flips between Points-of-Presence (PoPs) when short-lived latency spikes occur. Flapping increases tail latency for in-flight requests and causes unnecessary model-variant fallbacks. Goal: Implement a PoP selection orchestrator that uses both median and tail latency percentiles together with network-quality signals to compute a robust score per PoP, apply hysteresis to avoid churn, and surface deterministic fallback model-variant choices when the selected PoP is degraded.
design_summary: Compute a composite PoP score S = w_m * norm(p50) + w_t * norm(p95) + w_n * net_penalty, where norm() is a bounded normalized latency score and net_penalty is a penalty derived from recent packet-loss, TCP retransmit ratio, and 1-minute jitter. Use dual-quantile signals (median + tail) to capture both typical and worst-case behavior. Apply an exponential-time hysteresis window so PoP switches only occur when new PoP exceeds current by margin M for T_switch seconds. Maintain an escrow budget per PoP to limit aggressive fallbacks: if a PoP's escrow < threshold, prefer secondary PoPs or a lower-tier model variant. Default weights: w_m=0.35, w_t=0.45, w_n=0.20; margin M=3% relative score; T_switch=30s. This ticket scopes the scoring function, hysteresis rules, escrow model, and API surface for rollout metadata. Implementation will expose metrics and decision traces in Console for debugging and retrospective analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Score computation implemented and unit-tested (norm, net_penalty, weighted sum)
Hysteresis gating works end-to-end with synthetic traffic tests (no switch for <T_switch unless margin M exceeded)
Escrow budget prevents >2 switches/min for a single customer under noisy telemetry
Decision traces are visible in Console: per-request selected PoP, candidate PoPs and scores, hysteresis state
Canary rollout to 5% of traffic with automated rollback on SLO regression
Documentation PR describing config knobs, defaults, and recommended tuning published
implementation_steps: Add normalized latency calculators to telemetry ingestion (p50 & p95 moving windows)
Compute network-quality signal from packet loss & jitter telemetry and expose net_penalty metric
Build PoP scorer service (stateless evaluation; uses recent telemetry history)
Integrate hysteresis state machine in the router with time-decayed probation windows
Implement escrow accounting per-customer/PoP and fallback selection for model variants
Add decision tracing events to trace pipeline and Console UI hooks
Create synthetic load tests that inject noisy samples to validate hysteresis and escrow behavior
Canary rollout with automated SLO checks and manual override flag
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring math and normalization; integration tests using telemetry replayer to simulate injection of p50/p95 and packet-loss anomalies; chaos tests that simulate network partition to verify fallback variant selection; CI job that runs canary traffic against a staging PoP cluster and validates no SLO regressions. Post-deploy, run 72-hour telemetry audit and compare switch-rate and tail-latency to baseline.
observability_and_metrics: Expose per-PoP metrics: normalized_p50, normalized_p95, net_penalty, composite_score, hysteresis_state (Open/Locked/Probation), escrow_balance. Add derived dashboards: PoP-switch-rate, switches per customer per hour, median+tail latency delta around switch events, model-variant fallback frequency. Emit decision-trace logs with compact JSON for 1% of requests for sampling.
rollout_plan: 1) Roll core scoring service behind feature flag to internal traffic. 2) Enable decision traces for 0.5% of production requests. 3) Canary to 5% customer traffic with SLO guard rails. 4) Expand to 25% after 48h if no regressions. 5) Full rollout with configurable defaults and CAPI flag to opt-out.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overweighting p95 could cause persistent preference for higher-cost PoPs. Mitigation: cap p95 contribution and run cost-aware experiments (alternate weight set). Risk: telemetry freshness causing bad decisions. Mitigation: fall back to last-known-good PoP and mark telemetry-staleness in decision trace. Risk: escrow depletion causing suboptimal fallbacks. Mitigation: refill policy and per-customer soft-limits before hard failover.
open_questions: What is the best time-window for p95 smoothing to balance responsiveness vs noise? (15s, 30s, 60s?)
Should net_penalty include TCP retransmits or rely solely on packet-loss and jitter metrics?
How large should the initial escrow budget be for trial customers vs enterprise customers?
Do we allow customers to pin routing policy to 'latency-only' or 'cost-aware' modes?
